get.description: Tells a personal access token who it is: the user it acts as, its name, its scopes, the organizations it was limited to and when it expires. It says nothing about any organization, and it needs neither the `X-RootKey-Organization` header nor a scope. Only a personal access token can call it: a request with an API key gets the `404` that any path the API does not have gets.

400.description: An `x-api-key` sent together with `Authorization: Bearer rk_...` (`conflicting_credentials`).

401.description: Unauthenticated. A missing, malformed, unknown, inactive, revoked or expired credential all get the same answer.

403.description: The user has not verified their email address and the grace period has run out (`email_verification_required`).

429.description: Too many requests. The `Retry-After` header says how many seconds to wait. See [Rate Limits](/pages/rate-limits).

get.summary: List the organizations a token can act in
get.description: Lists the organizations the user belongs to that the token reaches, each with its agent mode and whether the user is blocked from agents there. Use it to choose the value of `X-RootKey-Organization`. An organization where agents are off, or where the user is blocked, is still listed, so you can tell the user why a request there is refused. An organization whose IP access rules block your network is left out. It needs no `X-RootKey-Organization` header. Only a personal access token can call it: a request with an API key gets the `404` that any path the API does not have gets.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `pagination.nextCursor` of the previous page. It is opaque; a cursor that is not valid gets `invalid_cursor`, never a restart from the first page.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: By creation time.

400.description: An invalid `limit` or `order` (`invalid_query_parameters`), a cursor that is not valid (`invalid_cursor`), or an `x-api-key` sent together with `Authorization: Bearer rk_...` (`conflicting_credentials`).

401.description: Unauthenticated. A missing, malformed, unknown, inactive, revoked or expired credential all get the same answer.

429.description: Too many requests. The `Retry-After` header says how many seconds to wait. See [Rate Limits](/pages/rate-limits).

get.summary: Get the organization a token acts in
get.description: Returns the organization named by `X-RootKey-Organization` as the token sees it: its name, its agent mode and the scopes the token effectively has there. It needs the `rootkey.read` scope. When the organization does not allow the request, the answer is the `403` whose `errorCode` says why, so this is the call to make first to find out whether a token can work in an organization. Only a personal access token can call it: a request with an API key gets the `404` that any path the API does not have gets.

200.description: The organization as the token sees it

400.description: The `X-RootKey-Organization` header is missing (`organization_header_required`), or an `x-api-key` sent together with `Authorization: Bearer rk_...` (`conflicting_credentials`).

401.description: Unauthenticated. A missing, malformed, unknown, inactive, revoked or expired credential all get the same answer.

404.description: An API key was used: this endpoint is for personal access tokens.

429.description: Too many requests. The `Retry-After` header says how many seconds to wait. See [Rate Limits](/pages/rate-limits).

get.description: Lists the vaults of your organization (the ones that hold files), newest first. With an API key it lists every vault of the organization, in the test or live data of the key. With a personal access token it lists what the user sees in the ROOTKey app: the vaults of the user's teams in the organization named by `X-RootKey-Organization` (every vault of the organization for an owner or an administrator), on the data `x-test-mode` selects. A vault that an IP access rule hides from your network is left out of the page and of `metadata.totalCount`. A RESTRICTED vault is listed with `agentAccessible: false` when a personal access token asks, and no agent can read or change it. A personal access token needs the `rootkey.read` scope.

post.description: Uploads a file and anchors its hash to create a verifiable record. The file becomes part of the specified vault. The file travels in this request; for large files, or to register many files, use a [direct upload](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/direct-uploads) instead. A personal access token with the `rootkey.write` scope can call it, in an organization that lets agents write.

ownerVault.description: Address of the vault that will own the file

expirationDate.description: Optional expiry date-time for the smart contract

post.description: Starts a direct upload: you declare the file's name, size and SHA-256, and ROOTKey answers with a signed URL (or a part plan, for a large file) to send the bytes to. Nothing is anchored and nothing is consumed from your plan until you [complete the upload](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/complete-file-upload). Read [Direct file uploads](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/direct-uploads) first for the whole flow. A personal access token with the `rootkey.write` scope can call it, in an organization that lets agents write.

ownerVault.description: Address of the vault that will own the file. `ownerWallet` is accepted as an alias.

fileName.description: The file's name, with its extension. This is the name the file shows in the vault.

size.description: The file's size in bytes. The bytes you upload must be exactly this long.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the whole file, as 64 hexadecimal characters. This is the hash that gets anchored.

contentType.description: The file's media type. ROOTKey keeps it for types that browsers do not execute (PDF, images, plain text, CSV, JSON, archives, office documents, audio and video) and stores anything else as `application/octet-stream`. The `Content-Type` in the response says which.

parentId.description: Upload a new version of this file instead of a new file. The file must be in the same vault.

expirationDate.description: Optional expiry date-time for the smart contract

201.description: Upload started. `mode` says how to send the bytes: `single` carries one signed URL, `multipart` carries a part plan.

400.description: The request failed a check: a malformed body, an invalid vault address, a paused vault, or a plan limit (`usage_limit_exceeded`).

404.description: The vault or the parent file does not exist in your organization (`resource_not_found`), or direct uploads are not available on this deployment (`presigned_file_upload_disabled`).

413.description: `file_too_large`: the file is larger than the 5 GiB maximum.

429.description: Your organization has too much open at once, and nothing was created: `too_many_open_file_uploads` or `too_many_open_file_upload_bytes`. Complete or abort some uploads ([list them](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/list-file-uploads)), or wait for them to expire, then try again. A `429` with `rate_limit_exceeded` is the rate limit instead: see the `Retry-After` header.

get.description: Lists the uploads that API keys of your organization have open: started and not yet completed or expired, or waiting for verification. Use it to find an upload your client lost track of and abort it. The `metadata.organization` block shows what your whole organization has open, which is what the open-upload limits judge. Not available to personal access tokens or agents: a request that carries one is refused with `agent_route_not_available`. Use an API key, or the ROOTKey app.

get.description: Returns the state of an upload. Poll it after completing a multipart upload, until `status` is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`. A personal access token with the `rootkey.write` scope can call it, in an organization that lets agents write.

parameters.name: uploadId
parameters.description: The `uploadId` returned by [Start an upload](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/start-file-upload).

404.description: `file_upload_not_found`: no such upload in your organization. An upload of another organization gets the same answer.

delete.description: Aborts an upload that has not been completed, and deletes what was uploaded for it. Repeating the call is harmless. Abort the uploads you will not finish: an open upload counts against your organization's open-upload limits until it ends. A personal access token with the `rootkey.write` scope can call it, in an organization that lets agents write.

parameters.name: uploadId
parameters.description: The `uploadId` returned by [Start an upload](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/start-file-upload).

409.description: `file_upload_not_open`: the upload is already being completed, or it is finished.

post.description: For a `multipart` upload only: returns one signed URL for each part you name, up to 100 per call. Each URL is signed for that part's exact length (`partSize`, or the remainder for the last part) and lives for a few minutes, so request them shortly before you send the parts. A personal access token with the `rootkey.write` scope can call it, in an organization that lets agents write.

parameters.name: uploadId
parameters.description: The `uploadId` returned by [Start an upload](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/start-file-upload).

partNumber.description: From 1 to the `partCount` of the upload.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of this part alone, as 64 hexadecimal characters. Always sending it is safe: it is required where the storage checks each part as it arrives (`file_upload_part_checksum_required` otherwise), and ignored where it cannot.

409.description: `file_upload_not_open`: the upload is no longer open.

410.description: `file_upload_expired`: the upload expired. Start a new one.

post.description: Tells ROOTKey the bytes are uploaded. ROOTKey checks them against the SHA-256 you declared, then anchors the hash and creates the file. For a `single` upload the answer is `200`, with the same fields as [Create file](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/create-file) plus `fileId`. For a `multipart` upload the answer is `202`: the whole file is verified first, and you poll [the upload](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/get-file-upload) until it is `COMPLETED`. This is the call that consumes one file and one API request from your plan. Repeating it is safe: a completed upload answers with its file again, and an upload that is being completed is never anchored twice. A personal access token with the `rootkey.write` scope can call it, in an organization that lets agents write.

parameters.name: uploadId
parameters.description: The `uploadId` returned by [Start an upload](/api-reference/platform/endpoint/files/start-file-upload).

200.description: The file was created and its anchor submitted (`single` uploads).

202.description: Accepted (`multipart` uploads): the whole file's SHA-256 is being verified before anything is anchored.

400.description: A plan limit (`usage_limit_exceeded`) or a paused vault. The upload stays open, so you can repeat the call once it is resolved.

409.description: `file_upload_incomplete` (the bytes are not all there yet), `file_upload_finalizing` (the upload is already being completed: check its status, then try again), `file_upload_not_open` (it is finished, failed or aborted), or `no_promotable_version`.

410.description: `file_upload_expired`: the upload expired. Start a new one.

422.description: `file_upload_checksum_mismatch` or `file_upload_size_mismatch`: what was stored is not what you declared. The upload fails and what was stored is deleted. Start a new one.

500.description: `creation_outcome_unknown` (the anchor may or may not exist: do not repeat the upload, see [Errors](/api-reference/errors#creation_outcome_unknown)) or `internal_error`.

post.description:
Creates a structured, integrity-hashed record inside a **table**.

**This endpoint also creates versions.** ROOTKey groups a record's versions by the table's **primary key** — the schema's key column, which (until one is explicitly designated) is the **first field**, by convention an `id`.

- If **no record with that key value exists yet**, the payload is stored as a new **root** record.
- If a **record with the same key value already exists**, the payload is stored as a **new version** of that entity (a database-style update). The version's `parentId` is set to the existing root automatically — you do not send it.

So to update an entity, simply `POST` the same primary key again — there is **no separate version-creation endpoint**; versioning is a built-in behaviour of this route.

Versioning only applies when the table has a schema **and** the payload is a keyed object with a non-empty key value; otherwise the record is stored as a standalone root.

**Response:** returns only `{ chainId }`. The new record's `id` is **not** returned here — read it from `GET /platform/records` (the `__meta.id` field of each item). A personal access token with the `rootkey.write` scope can call it, in an organization that lets agents write.

200.description: Record created (or a new version, if its primary key already existed)

401.description: Unauthenticated — missing or invalid API key

get.description:
Returns the version history of a record, newest first by default. `parentId` is the record's `id` (from the `__meta.id` field of a List Records item). Each item is a full record version including its decrypted column values in `data`.

**Response shape:** this endpoint returns a bare pagination envelope (`data` / `pagination` / `metadata`) — unlike List Records and Fetch Record History, there is **no `chainId` wrapper**. A personal access token with the `rootkey.read` scope can call it.

parameters.name: parentId
parameters.description: The record `id` whose versions to list (a branch root's id).

parameters.name: vaultAddress
parameters.description: Address of the table that owns the record.

404.description: Record not found (or not owned by the caller's table)

get.description: Returns the activity/audit log for a record — creation, new versions, deletion, and related events — newest first by default. `fileId` is the record's `id` (from `__meta.id`). A personal access token with the `rootkey.read` scope can call it.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The record `id` whose history to fetch.

get.description:
Returns the integrity-validation history for a record — each entry compares the stored payload against its integrity hash. `fileId` is the record's `id` (from `__meta.id`).

**Response shape:** returned directly with **no `chainId` wrapper** — `{ currentHash, previousHash, validations }`, where `currentHash`/`previousHash` are the hashes of the current and parent-version payloads. A personal access token with the `rootkey.read` scope can call it.

parameters.name: fileId
parameters.description: The record `id` whose validations to fetch.

200.description: Current & previous hashes plus paginated validations

x-api-key.name: x-api-key
x-api-key.description: ROOTKey API key. A test key works on your organization's test data and a live key on its live data; both are used with the same API.

personalAccessToken.description: Personal access token of a ROOTKey user, sent as `Authorization: Bearer rk_pat_...`. A token acts as the user who created it, in the organization named by the `X-RootKey-Organization` header, and never with more access than that user has in the ROOTKey app: the organization's agent policy, the user's own role and teams, and the token's scopes (`rootkey.read`, `rootkey.write`, `rootkey.delete`) all apply. A missing, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired token gets the same `401`. Send either an `x-api-key` or a bearer token, never both: a request with both gets `conflicting_credentials`. See [Authentication](/api-reference/auth).

DomainError.description: Domain-level error (validation or a business rule violation)

AgentAccessDenied.description: Forbidden. With a personal access token or an app connected through the hosted connector, the organization, the user or the token does not allow the request, and the `errorCode` says which: `agent_org_not_allowed`, `agent_user_blocked`, `agent_two_factor_required`, `agent_access_disabled`, `agent_write_not_allowed`, `agent_personal_tokens_disabled`, `agent_client_not_allowed`, `insufficient_scope`, `insufficient_permission`, `agent_restricted_data_denied` or `email_verification_required`. A user who is not a member of the organization, or a network an IP access rule blocks, gets `access_policy_denied`. Each code has an entry on the [Errors](/api-reference/errors) page.

records.description: Paginated records — each item's top-level fields are the record's decrypted column values (dynamic, per the table schema), plus a reserved `__meta` object carrying the record's identifiers.

ownership.description: Whether the submitting party owns the anchored file

integrity.description: Whether the file hash matches the anchored hash

validity.description: Whether the smart contract is still valid (not expired or revoked)

reportId.description: ID of the created compliance report

status.description: Initial status; the report is processed asynchronously

chainId.description: Polygon chain ID (137 in production, 80002 on Amoy testnet)

transactionHash.description: On-chain transaction hash of the anchoring transaction

ownerVault.description: Address of the table that will own the record. (`ownerWallet` is accepted as an alias.)

recordData.description: The record's columns as a JSON object. Values are primitives (string, number, boolean, ISO date, null) or nested objects/arrays within limits: 1 MB per record, 64 KB per string, 100 properties, 10 levels of nesting, 1,000 array elements. Keys beginning with `__` (and prototype-polluting keys) are stripped on ingest. The value of the schema's key column (the primary key) determines version grouping — see the endpoint description.

expirationDate.description: Optional expiry date-time for the record.

CreateRecordResponse.description: Record create/version response. Note: unlike files, record creation does not return a `transactionHash` or the new record `id` — obtain the id from `GET /platform/records` (`__meta.id`).

chainId.description: Polygon chain ID (137 in production, 80002 on the Amoy testnet).

RecordMeta.description: Reserved metadata envelope attached to every List Records item. `__`-prefixed keys are stripped from user data on ingest, so this never collides with a user-defined column.

id.description: The record's unique id — use as `parentId` for versions and as `recordId` for history / validations / delete.

parentId.description: The branch root's id when this record is a version; null for a root record.

status.description: Anchoring status (uppercase). Note: the List Records `status` query filter takes the lowercase form — `pending` / `registered` / `error`.

RecordListItem.description: A record as returned by List Records: the record's decrypted column values spread at the top level (dynamic, per the table schema), plus a reserved `__meta` object.

memberId.description: Organization member who created this version; null when created via API key.

blockchainId.description: On-chain identifier; null for records (records are integrity-hashed, not blockchain-anchored).

transactionHash.description: Always null for records — records are not submitted to the blockchain.

dataHash.description: Integrity hash of the record payload.

data.description: The decrypted column values of this record version.

databse.description: NOTE: source key is misspelled `databse` (see VerifyAppHealth use case)

UpdateTrustSettingsBody.description: All fields optional. Only present fields are applied. The trust page logo mirrors the organisation logo, set via the organisation profile use case — it is NOT writable here.

url.description: Send the bytes to this URL.

headers.description: Send exactly these headers. They are part of the signature, so a different value is refused by the storage. The object can be empty. Your HTTP client sets `Content-Length` itself.

expiresAt.description: The request must start before this time.

fileId.description: The id the file will have once the upload is completed.

status.description: `PENDING`: waiting for the bytes or for you to complete it. `VERIFYING`: a multipart upload being checked. `FINALIZING`: being anchored. `COMPLETED`: the file exists. `FAILED`: see `failureCode`. `EXPIRED`, `ABORTED`: ended without a file.

name.description: The name the user gave the token.

allOrganizations.description: True when the token covers every organization the user belongs to, now and later.

organizationIds.description: The organizations the token was limited to. Empty when `allOrganizations` is true.

AgentOrganizationMode.description: What the organization lets agents do: `DISABLED` serves no agent request, `READ_ONLY` only reads, `FULL` reads, writes and deletes. An organization that never saved a policy is `READ_ONLY`.

blocked.description: True when an administrator of the organization blocked this user from agents. The organization is still listed: the user belongs to it.

effectiveScopes.description: The token's own scopes narrowed by what the organization allows now: none when agents are disabled, when the user is blocked, when the organization requires two-factor authentication and the user has none, or when it does not allow personal access tokens; only `rootkey.read` (when the token has it) in a read-only organization; the token's scopes otherwise. It never adds a scope the token does not hold. The user's role can still refuse an individual request.

VaultOrTableListItem.description: One row of the vault or table listing.

address.description: The vault or table address, as the other endpoints take it.

agentAccessible.description: Only in the answer to a personal access token. False for a RESTRICTED vault or table: it is listed so that an agent can tell the user it exists, and every endpoint that would read or change it is refused with `agent_restricted_data_denied`. True for every other classification.

OrganizationHeader.name: X-RootKey-Organization
OrganizationHeader.description: The organization a personal access token acts in: the `id` of one of the organizations that `GET /organizations` lists. Required with a personal access token on every endpoint that works inside an organization; without it the request gets `organization_header_required`. Ignored with an API key, which belongs to exactly one organization.

TestModeHeader.name: x-test-mode
TestModeHeader.description: Whether a personal access token works on live data (`false`, the default) or on test data (`true`). Only this header decides, never a query string or a body field. An API key is itself a test or a live key and works on that data.
